changes.before: The speaker links his wife’s appearance and age with his judgment of her public sociability. The complexion praise and gendered reproach belong to that source voice. They are not this edition’s standards for women’s worth or conduct. ଧନ is read as an address meaning dear; the verse itself supplies no punctuation to resolve that reading independently.
changes.after: The speaker links his wife’s appearance and age with his judgment of her public sociability. The complexion praise and gendered reproach belong to that source voice. They are not this edition’s standards for women’s worth or conduct. ଧନ is an affectionate address, “dear,” within the speaker’s direct appeal to his wife.
changes.reason: Full dictionary explicitly supports spouse vocative; remove unnecessary punctuation-based doubt.
